Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot is a common disease in pepper plants caused by Xanthomonas bacteria. It appears as small, water-soaked spots that turn dark brown or black with yellow halos. Severe infection can cause leaf drop and reduce fruit quality.
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves immediately. Avoid overhead watering. Apply copper-based bactericides. Use disease-resistant seeds and practice crop rotation.

Pepper__bell___healthy.description: The pepper plant is healthy with no visible signs of disease. Leaves are green, firm, and free from spots or discoloration.
Pepper__bell___healthy.treatment: Maintain proper watering, sunlight, and nutrient balance. Regularly inspect plants to prevent early disease infection.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Early blight is a fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani. It shows as dark brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves, leading to yellowing and leaf drop.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Remove affected leaves and apply fungicides like chlorothalonil. Maintain proper spacing and avoid excessive moisture.

Potato___healthy.description: The potato plant is healthy with no signs of disease. Leaves appear green and vigorous.
Potato___healthy.treatment: Continue proper care, watering, and fertilization. Monitor regularly for early signs of infection.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Late blight is a serious disease caused by Phytophthora infestans. It causes large dark lesions on leaves and stems, often leading to rapid plant decay.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Remove infected plants immediately. Apply fungicides such as mancozeb. Avoid wet conditions and ensure proper drainage.

Tomato__Target_Spot.description: Target spot is a fungal disease characterized by circular brown spots with concentric rings on leaves and fruit.
Tomato__Target_Spot.treatment: Use fungicides and remove infected plant parts. Improve air circulation and avoid high humidity.

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: Tomato mosaic virus causes mottled light and dark green patches on leaves, distortion, and reduced fruit yield.
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: Remove infected plants immediately. Disinfect tools and avoid handling plants when wet. Use resistant varieties.

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.description: This viral disease causes yellowing, leaf curling, and stunted growth. It is spread by whiteflies.
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.treatment: Control whiteflies using insecticides or traps. Remove infected plants and use resistant varieties.

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial spot appears as small dark lesions on leaves, stems, and fruits. It reduces yield and fruit quality.
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper sprays and avoid overhead irrigation. Use disease-free seeds and practice crop rotation.

Tomato_Early_blight.description: Early blight in tomatoes causes brown spots with ring patterns on leaves, leading to yellowing and defoliation.
Tomato_Early_blight.treatment: Remove infected leaves and apply fungicides. Maintain good spacing and avoid wet foliage.

Tomato_healthy.description: The tomato plant is healthy with green leaves and no visible disease symptoms.
Tomato_healthy.treatment: Maintain proper watering, sunlight, and fertilization.

Tomato_Late_blight.description: Late blight is a severe disease causing large dark patches on leaves and fruit rot, especially in wet conditions.
Tomato_Late_blight.treatment: Remove infected plants and apply fungicides. Avoid high humidity and improve air circulation.

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.description: Leaf mold is caused by fungus and appears as yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces with mold underneath.
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.treatment: Reduce humidity and improve ventilation. Apply fungicides and avoid overcrowding plants.

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.description: Septoria leaf spot causes small circular spots with gray centers and dark edges. It spreads rapidly in humid conditions.
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves and apply fungicides. Avoid watering leaves directly.

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.description: Spider mites are tiny pests that suck sap from leaves, causing yellow speckles and webbing.
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.treatment: Spray water to remove mites and use insecticidal soap or neem oil. Maintain plant humidity.
